data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemeni army claims 1,540 Houthi casualties as fighting intensifies in Taiz
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Yemeni army claims 1,540 Houthi casualties as fighting intensifies in Taiz
The Yemeni government has claimed that 1,540 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded during the past 24 hours as the battles raging in the southwestern governorate of Taiz intensified.
The Yemeni army said it carried out 474 operations against Houthi positions, reinforcements, command centres and military capabilities across several fronts, with most of the reported casualties concentrated in Taiz.
Military spokesman Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili said that the raids included warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and rocket launchers.
The latest claims come as Taiz heats up as one of the main battlegrounds in Yemen's renewed conflict.
Government forces have reported repeated clashes across the province in recent weeks, including around Bani Bakari, Maqbanah, al-Aqroud and the northern and eastern approaches to Taiz city.
Read more: Yemeni army claims 1,540 Houthi casualties as fighting intensifies in Taiz

According to the sources, Mohammad Talat Aqel, from Jabalia refugee camp died after sustaining a gunshot wound to the head several days ago in the Umm Dhuhair area of Deir al-Balah. He was reportedly receiving treatment at the city's Al-Aqsa Hospital.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Eight Palestinians, including mother and daughter, killed in attacks across Gaza since dawn
data.author: Katherine Hearst
data.summary:
Eight Palestinians, including mother and daughter, killed in attacks across Gaza since dawn
Eight Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza since dawn, Al Jazeera reports, citing medical sources.
Five people were killed in an Israeli attack on a residential block in Gaza City, including one in Beit Lahia, while two others succumbed to wounds sustained in previous attacks.
Wafa news agency reported earlier that Muhammad Talaat Aqel succumbed to a gunshot wound to his head, which he had sustained in an attack days before.
Reuters reports that four women were among the five killed in the apartment block attack. Medics and the local church reported that Maisa Abu Dawoud, and her daughter Mary, were among the victims. The attack reportedly levelled the building, causing a fire to rip through the debris.
"We were asleep and suddenly heard continuous strikes and heavy explosions. The children woke up startled and started running and screaming," witness Ahmed Al-Dahdouh told Reuters.
"We ran out and found that our neighbour's house was struck and there were dismembered martyrs, women, men and children. We started to pull them out. They were scattered under the rubble," he said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Iranian rial at new low, as cenbank sells dollars to support currency
Iran's rial continued its decline on Saturday, as the central bank announced an injection of up to $2 billion to support the currency while the economy faces US sanctions and a naval blockade.
The US dollar was sold at around 2.688 million rials, up from 2.632 million on Friday, according to free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, while alanchand.com reported 2.695 million rials per dollar.
State television said state banks began selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value in the past year.
With an inflation rate of more than 70 percent, life is becoming ever tougher for ordinary citizens unable to afford basic necessities or rent ​as a US blockade cuts the state's financial lifeline – oil exports.
Many Iranians seeking safe havens for their savings have been buying dollars, other hard currencies or gold.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Yemeni forces say strikes conducted against Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada
data.author: Hilal Saki
data.summary:
Yemeni forces say strikes conducted against Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada
Yemen's armed forces said early on Sunday it was conducting strikes against the Houthis in the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada.
A spokesperson for Yemen's armed forces, which are aligned with the internationally recognised government, said forces were targeting what he described as "vital targets", without providing further details.
Yemen's Houthi-run Al Masirah TV reported earlier an attack it said was carried out by Saudi Arabia on Sanaa. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation on the report.
The conflict between the Iran-backed Houthis and forces aligned with the Saudi-backed government mostly stopped after a 2022 truce, but fighting has broken out again in a spillover from the wider war between Iran and the United States.
Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Saudi Arabia has responded with air strikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to repel the Houthis.

data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
Iran welcomes exit of US forces from Iraq, calls for Washington to be held accountable
Iran’s foreign ministry on Saturday has congratulated the Iraqi government and people on the exit of US and other foreign forces from Iraq.
In a statement posted on its Telegram channel, the ministry said the withdrawal is “a very important and necessary step” towards consolidating Iraq’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence.
It accused the US of causing “irreparable consequences” for Iraq and the region since the 2003 invasion, which it said was launched under the false pretext of “weapons of mass destruction”, and called for the US government to be held accountable for crimes committed during the occupation.

data.title: Middle East Eye: State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US
data.author: Bilge Kotan
data.summary:
State Department says Iranian UN delegation duo expelled from US
The United States has expelled two members of the Iranian delegation who attended the recent UN General Assembly after they ignored an order to leave the country, the State Department said Saturday.
"Two more members of the Iranian delegation were found still in (New York) long after the United Nations General Assembly had passed. They have now been kicked out of the US," a US official told AFP, adding that Secretary of State Marco Rubio "means business."
US media reported the State Department had told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation to leave the country Monday, and resorted to expelling the two members after learning from the Iranian mission to the UN they remained in the country on Friday.
One member of the delegation left Friday night, while the second departed Saturday morning, according to Axios.
